## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the test prints 11 `ok` lines at the PR head and on the current `quattro` tip (the PR merges cleanly), both directly and through `./test/shell`. The 15 derived commands match the 15 ledger entries exactly, and each is a real comparison of that command's output against a literal. The add-a-crossing and remove-the-weather-comparison demonstrations fail as described. `bash --dump-po-strings` parses without executing (bash 5.3 and 3.2.57 `shell.c`), reports none of the 13 `$"` regex anchors in `bin/`, and catches a real marker.

The notes below concern how much the two checks cover compared with what the ledger header and description promise. No shipped behavior is affected.

### The translation check covers only markers inside `bin/<command>`

The ledger header says protocol output must never be marked for translation and that "the test enforces that". The check runs `bash --dump-po-strings` and `\bgettext\b|\beval_gettext\b` over `bin/<command>` only. Several protocol vocabularies are produced elsewhere, or marked by functions the check does not recognize. Results below come from the unmodified test run against mutations of a private copy of the merged tree; each "no" row passed with 11 `ok` lines. The QML row is from source reading.

| Where the vocabulary could be translated | Caught? |
|---|---|
| `$"Custom"` inside `bin/omarchy-dns` | yes |
| `omarchy-transcode` passing `$"high" $"medium" $"low"` to `omarchy-menu-select`, then `case "$resolution" in high) ...` | no, the options belong to the caller |
| `omarchy-shell` replies (`ok`, `not ready`, `could not find target widget ...`) built in `shell/shell.qml` / `PluginRegistry.qml`, compared in `omarchy-bar` and `omarchy-menu-images` | no, QML is not scanned (source reading) |
| `omarchy_t "Custom"` (the helper proposed in #8765) in `omarchy-dns` | no |
| `ngettext` in `omarchy-dns`, `eval_ngettext` in `omarchy-channel-current` | no |
| A comment containing the word `gettext` in `omarchy-dns` | flagged as a marker, with only the file path in the message |

**Impact:** an i18n change can break a protocol vocabulary with this test still green, while a harmless comment fails it.

**Suggested change:** state in the header exactly what is checked. Note in the `omarchy-menu-select` and `omarchy-shell` entries where their vocabularies originate. Extend the word check to GNU gettext's full shell set (`ngettext`, `eval_ngettext`, `eval_pgettext`, `eval_npgettext`), match command positions rather than any occurrence, and print the matching line. If #8765's helper lands, add `omarchy_t`/`omarchy_tn`.

### Any marker anywhere in a protocol command fails, including stderr text

Changing `echo "Error: No DNS servers provided." >&2` to `echo $"Error: ..." >&2` in `bin/omarchy-dns` fails the test (`omarchy-dns	marks a string with $"..."`), although stdout is unchanged. The same applies to prompts, usage text and notifications in the other 13 protocol commands. Whole-file scope is sometimes right: `omarchy-bar` matches `omarchy-shell`'s stderr sentences `not ready` / `is not running`.

**Impact:** the first i18n PR to translate an error message in one of these files will hit a failure the ledger does not explain.

**Suggested change:** decide this deliberately. Either say in the header that no string in a protocol file may be marked, or narrow the check to the strings that reach parsed output.

### The derivation is a line pattern, so the ledger can still drift

"A hand-written list would rot; this one cannot" is stronger than the matching supports. Comparison shapes appended to a private copy of `bin/omarchy-ascii`:

```text
Derived (fails as undeclared)          Not derived (passes silently)
[[ $(omarchy-x) == "Custom" ]]         [[ $(omarchy-x) == 'Custom' ]]
[[ $(omarchy-x) == Custom ]]           [[ $(omarchy-x) == 0 ]]   /  == "0"
[[ 'Custom' == $(omarchy-x) ]]         [[ $(omarchy-x) == *Custom* ]]
case $(omarchy-x) in ...               [[ $(omarchy-x) =~ ^Custom$ ]]
v=$(omarchy-x); [[ $v == "Custom" ]]   [ "$(omarchy-x)" = "Custom" ]
                                       v=$( omarchy-x )  /  v=$(timeout 2 omarchy-x)
                                       read -r v < <(omarchy-x); [[ $v == "Custom" ]]
                                       omarchy-x | grep -qx Custom
```

The same single-quoted comparison is caught with the command on the right and missed with it on the left. The tree already has a multi-line case: `bin/omarchy-menu-images:341-352` captures `omarchy-shell image-selector open` across lines and then checks `!= "ok"`. It stays covered only because other `omarchy-shell` callers are derived. False positives also occur: a commented-out comparison, or `[[ -n $(omarchy-x) && $mode == "dark" ]]` (the 40-character window reaches the other comparison), each demand a ledger entry.

**Impact:** a new boundary written in one of the missed shapes lands unclassified, and some non-boundaries force entries.

**Suggested change:** reword the claim to the shapes actually derived, and list the known blind spots in the ledger header. Optionally, accept single-quoted and numeric right-hand sides, `=~`, and glob patterns, and skip comment lines.

### Ledger entries: vocabulary accuracy and uniqueness

- `omarchy-theme-color`: the derived caller compares `light`/`dark` (`bin/omarchy-theme-set-gnome:18-20`), which the vocabulary text does not list.
- `omarchy-shell`: "usually JSON" does not describe the status tokens callers compare (`ok`, `not ready`, and English error sentences).
- The third field is not checked: an empty vocabulary passes, and so do duplicate or conflicting rows (`omarchy-dns	protocol` plus `omarchy-dns	prose`), because `ledger_field` deduplicates with `sort -u`. A uniqueness check on `$1` would close this.

**Test notes:** the guard at line 57, `(( $(printf '%s\n' "$declared" | wc -l) > 0 ))`, cannot fail, because `printf` always emits a newline; `[[ -n $declared ]]` expresses the intent. Without `rg` (or without PCRE2), the first failure is reported as "the ledger records no boundary that has gone away", listing all 15; `require_command rg` from `base-test.sh` would give a direct message.
